content: Heinrich Heine University, officially known as the Heinrich Heine University of Düsseldorf, is a higher education institution located in Düsseldorf, Germany. The university is named after Heinrich Heine, a renowned German poet and political thinker who was born in Düsseldorf in 1797. Since 1965, it has operated as a fully established university, currently comprising faculties of law, medicine, philosophy, mathematics and natural sciences, and economics. The university has an enrollment of slightly over 18,000 students. The current rector is Prof. Dr. Dr. A. (Soz.). In 1806, Joachim Murat, Napoleon Bonaparte's brother-in-law and the ruler of the Duchy of Berg, expressed the intention to establish a university in Düsseldorf. At that time, only a few college-like institutions existed, having developed between the 16th and 18th centuries. On December 12, 1811, Napoleon issued a decree calling for the establishment of a university with five faculties in the duchy. However, the French invasion of Russia hindered the realization of this plan. In 1907, a medical academy was founded in Düsseldorf, and by 1923, it began training students. In 1962, the state of North Rhine-Westphalia assumed responsibility for the academy from the city of Düsseldorf. Subsequently, in 1965, the state government decided to transform the medical academy into a university. On January 1, 1966, the university was officially established with a faculty of medicine and a combined faculty for natural sciences and philosophy. An opening ceremony was held on February 14 of the same year. The central campus buildings, located in the southern part of Düsseldorf, were completed in the 1970s, reflecting the architectural style of that era. Initially, the university was not named after Heinrich Heine due to longstanding controversies. Heine was considered an unsuitable figurehead, first for pragmatic reasons and later for political ones. It was not until December 20, 1988, that the university's senate decided to name the institution after Düsseldorf's most famous son. The university has awarded honorary degrees to notable individuals, including Johannes Rau, former President of the Federal Republic of Germany; Paul Spiegel, former President of the Central Council of Jews in Germany; and Marcel Reich-Ranicki, a prominent literary critic. Heinrich Heine University maintains partnerships with several international universities, including the University of Nantes (France), the University of Naples Federico II (Italy), Peking University (China), the University of Alicante (Spain), the University of Reading (UK), the University of California, Davis (USA), Pennsylvania State University (USA), Charles University in Prague (Czech Republic), and Keio University in Tokyo (Japan). Additionally, the university participates in numerous SOCRATES/ERASMUS partnerships.
